comments.body: FerretDB v1.10 added full support for the SQLite backend. We specifically tested it with FastNetMon. It would be nice to switch that PR to use SQLite.

Hello, FerretDB team member here. The FerretDB v1.10 is available in nixpkgs-unstable. What needs to be addressed to push this one forward? Is there anything I can help with? I see that the FerretDB module PR is stale, if that would help I can create module for the latest version / help with updating existing PR.

@noisersup I tried to integrate the sqlite backend into this PR, but I don't see a way to use sqlite backend with fastnetmon advanced because fastnetmon advanced has no (documented) option to disable authentication, while the sqlite backend does not support authentication.

So do we need to use `ferretdb` for this service ? Wouldn't it be more modular to have an option so the user can provide their mongodb compatible database url ? This way the user can choose between `ferretdb` and `mongodb`, and could also choose to have the database be remote ?

Usually the intention of a NixOS module is to make consumption as easy as possible for the majority of cases.
There are very few reasons that people would want to use an external MongoDB for this ephemeral configuration store (it gets cleared and repopulated on each start!).
If someone wants this, we can still add an option to disable ferretdb later.
Meanwhile, without some MongoDB implementation, fastnetmon-advanced won't be able to start, so it is an essential dependency that each user needs.

As background information on how fastnetmon advanced uses mongodb/ferretdb in a normal setup:

It is used for storing the configuration. literally nothing else. The database has one collection with one document, containing the fastnetmon configuration.

In our NixOS module, this database is completely emptied and replaced on each boot by the fastnetmon-setup service, to mimic a declarative configuration.
I also just built the package and ran the test on my machine, works like a charm!

review_comments.body: This should probably go in another module
There is a service for this in nixos

Unsure if it is applicable. fastnetmon and gobgp are tightly integrated. We use the (older) gobgp binaries that fastnetmon ships, and fastnetmon generates the gobgp config at runtime while the gobgp module does not provide a way to specify a config file path (it is always a declarative config living in the nix store).
Ah yes, I understand.

I created a ferretdb module here : https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/231138
Would be interested to have your feedback and know if it would fit your usecase
fastnetmon-advanced has upgraded its bundled gobgp version to 3.12 (so finally 3.x!). We could check if the latest 3.x works as well.
adding a link to the respective upstream options would be nice and adding examples even if you just copy paste the values from the nixosTest
If I understand correctly this just creates symlinks and fastnetmon creates those files at runtime? Btw what is the fastnetmon `license.lic`?
migrating this to a new version of fastnetmon that changes for example the database scheme seems like a really labor intensiv task.
this should probably be a configuration option and have the current values as defaults so user scan easily change the settings
this breaks as soon as anything else sets `security.polkit.extraConfig` because it's a string value and thus doesn't get merged, right or am I missing something?
the test currently doesn't test for stuff from `enableAdvancedTrafficPersistence` which you are likely using in prod so testing the option would probably be a nice touch.
It's `type = types.lines;`, which gets merged by concatenating all definitions with the same priority
what do you mean?

You understand correctly. We want these stateful files to be not in `/etc`.

`license.lic` is the cached fastnetmon advanced license. In fastnetmon advanced, a license is a assigned on the licensing server to an IP address. When fastnetmon advanced starts up, it attempts to obtain the license from the license server, and saves it to `/etc/fastnetmon/license.lic` which is valid for $TIME (14 days or so) until it has to obtain a renewed license. Think similar to how you would obtain TLS certificates over ACME and renew them periodically.
It's not really possible to test that without a license, and it is not a critical function (and we are using [NetMeta](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/232490) instead in prod ;))
Done
You can ignore my comment since the database only stores configuration which gets rebuild every start anyways. I was under the impression that it stores some state full data.

this is kinda ugly but I don't really see another way on how you would realize it since you said that chroot doesn't work, which should probably be stated in the comment above so if anyone in the future looks at the module again knows why you used `runInLinuxVm`

The content was converted to json before iirc but `settingsFormat` is set to `pkgs.formats.yaml` wouldn't this break because of this? As far as I'm aware json is a subset of yaml but not the other way around.

`(pkgs.formats.yaml {}).type` is the same as `(pkgs.formats.json {}).type`, since they share the same data model.
The real difference is the `.generate` function, which will produce nicely formatted json or yaml, but we don't use it for either
